# Detect Early, Repair Small

Prefer catching mistakes while blast radius is tiny over patching late under pressure.

## Stop signals

Treat these as pause-or-fix moments: verification disagrees with a recent write; an identifier you relied on does not exist; you are about to broadcast sensitive content widely.

## Repair sequence

Stabilize so nothing worse happens; isolate the failure with the smallest check; apply the smallest fix that restores consistency; re-verify at the real destination (file on disk, command output, service response).

## Retry policy

After two similar failures with the same tactic, switch tactic (different tool path, narrower write, different query).

## Learning hook

When recovery succeeds, log the failure class and the remedy pattern you will reuse—not the blow-by-blow story.
